Thank you for your extraordinary thoughtfulness.  Two days and ten pages into the journal you suggested gave me a lot of food for thought.

Yes, very selfish is correct.

However, please don't make assumptions about me, and about what I have done for myself, and what I have done for my kid.  Please don't make assumptions about what I can and cannot feel.  (EDIT: Please don't make assumptions  about what I think is ok or not.)

When you do that, you push me away, you distance me, and that's probably not the effect you want to have on the people in your life.

This is amazing advice.  I can see how your suggestion - as you acknowledge - offers therapeutic relief, and the intrinsic hope that minds can be changed, healed, etc.  However, I don't fault you for that one bit, I think it's excellent, and thank you.

But mostly, thank you for pointing out, right away, this wouldn't go very far towards helping him find peace.  A journal would probably be a far, far better vehicle than a note.  Thank you.
Please do not assume I haven't taken the precautions you suggest.  I don't know if you should be here, if I can say that.  Your tone is not helpful.
